rows.why: This scenario covers basic component summing. The only open question it settles is the `d` unit (rows `2d` and `1d0h0m0s0ms`). Item 1's pick accepts `d` as 86,400,000 ms, so `2d` gives 172800000. The zero-component rows also fit item 10's pick, which accepts them.
Item 4 asks whether whitespace is allowed at the ends. Its pick trims leading and trailing whitespace, so `  45m\n` parses to 2700000 with no error.

This is a mixed list of rejections. Several rows map to other items: empty (3), `90` (2), `1.5h` (5), `-3s` (6), `1h 30m` and `3 s` (4), `3S` (8), and all of those picks agree. Item 10 is the closest because it asks about leading zeros, which the `05s` row settles. Its pick accepts leading zeros (`01h`), but the scenario rejects `05s`.
No item asks whether a count can be larger than the next unit up (for example `90m` instead of `1h30m`). Item 7 is about unit order and repeats, not the size of a count.
Item 7 asks about units that are out of order or repeated. Its pick rejects any unit that is repeated or not in strictly descending order, which matches `30m1h`, `1h1h`, `1s500ms2s` and `5ms1s`.
Item 9 asks about the maximum duration. Its pick sets the cap at 2^53-1 ms and only rejects totals above it, so exactly 9007199254740991 parses.
Item 9's pick rejects totals above 2^53-1, including digit runs that would overflow int64, and returns an error with 0. Both rows are covered.

Item 11 asks how milliseconds are printed and which units are used. Its pick splits into d/h/m/s/ms, leaves out zero parts and uses days, which matches `1m30s`, `1d` and `1d1h1m1s1ms`. The `0ms` row is item 12, whose pick also agrees.
This tests the upper edge of the formatting range. Item 12's pick only errors for values above 2^53-1, so the largest value still formats. Item 11's format produces `104249991d8h59m991ms`.
No item asks whether formatting and then parsing gives back the original number.

Item 12 asks what formatting a negative or too-large value produces. Its pick returns an empty string with an error for negative values and for values above 2^53-1. That covers -1, 2^53, MinInt64 and MaxInt64.
